brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Bases on level 0 (piece:0,-1,0 full and piece:0,0,0 half-n) and on level 1 (piece:0,-1,1 full).
bin:0,-1,1~hex-bin-full-div3 is a three-way divided bin in the top-storey base.
drawer:0#0,0#cut is on the ground floor, on the cut face of the half base. It sits next to the upper storey rather than directly under it.
capOpenFaces added solid caps to every open face and check_build lists no OPEN_CAP_FACE; lockJoints bolted the joints.
The bin's three compartments hold screws, nuts and standoffs, and the drawer holds tweezers (props for staging only). The props are for show; nothing here can check how much the organizer can carry.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey workbench organizer with 25 parts. On the ground floor, a north-half base holds a drawer on its cut face, next to a full base. A second full base sits on top of that full base and holds a three-way divided bin. capOpenFaces added solid caps to every open face and lockJoints bolted the joints together. check_build shows no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. For staging, M3 screws, nuts and standoffs sit in the bin and tweezers sit in the drawer. Layout note: the upper storey stands on the full base only, so from above the drawer sits beside the bins rather than right under them.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
